title: A café floor in Penrose tiles
prompt: Draw a café floor tiled with a Penrose rhombus (P3) tiling, as an SVG.
groundTruth: The SVG rendered and judged by eye. A P3 tiling has two rhombi, one with a 72° and one with a 36° corner, and no shift maps it onto itself.

checks.label: Two rhombi, two fills
checks.how: Thick and thin rhombi, each in its own fill.
checks.rule: Pass if there are two rhombus shapes and every thick one is filled differently from every thin one.

checks.label: No repeat
checks.how: No translation maps the pattern onto itself.
checks.rule: Pass if no patch of the floor can be slid onto another so that the tiles line up. A rhombus grid in Penrose colours fails it.

checks.label: Fivefold, edges drawn
checks.how: Fivefold symmetry about the centre, with the tile edges drawn.
checks.rule: Pass if the floor looks the same turned a fifth of a turn about its centre and the tile edges are drawn.

harder: Ask for the matching rule as well, the arcs on each tile that force the tiling, so the edges have to meet the way P3 requires.

saturated.why: Pareto 26.10 Preview and GPT-6.1 Sol both drew a real P3 tiling in all three runs, and I passed all six by eye. Sol did it for about 9 cents a run and Pareto for 17 to 37.
